newsitem.title: CHINA: China central debt depository starts operations.
newsitem.headline: China central debt depository starts operations.

text.p: China's central state debt depository has begun partial operations with local exchanges and state debt trading centres shifting their positions to the depository, the China Securities newspaper said on Tuesday.

The Beijing-based depository, the China Government Securities Depository Trust and Clearing Co, was set up in February to co-ordinate all debt trading and is responsible for holding, clearing and settling all state debt transactions.
Beijing has ordered all local exchanges and state debt trading centres to shift their state debt positions to the central depository.
The newspaper said the Shanghai stock exchange has transferred 14 billion yuan ($1.7 billion) in state debt positions to the depository and the Shenzhen exchange three billion yuan ($361.7 million).
The depository will shortly begin full operations after co-ordination with the exchanges and local trading centres is completed, the newspaper said.

Last Saturday, Beijing issued new rules for state debt trading, saying positions placed with the central depository could be traded on any debt exchange and trading centre around the country with a receipt issued by the depository.
Previously, debt purchased in Shanghai, Shenzhen and Wuhan, the three main debt trading centres, could only be traded in the exchange where they were purchased.
